Brian Eno: The Man Who Fell to Earth 19711977 (2.5 hour Comprehensive documentary on one of the most influential artists of the 20th Century)

For those unaware, Eno began his professional music career with the influential glam band Roxy Music. He left rather quickly and went on to become an unparalleled innovator in music production as well as a prolific recording & visual artist. He is a highly recognized figure in pioneering electronic music, and is credit as the creator of "ambient" music. He helped save David Bowie's career by moving with him to Berlin where they produced 3 albums (known as the Berlin Trilogy) that resulted in Bowie getting off drugs and moving him into a highly experimental direction. Eno's production work is legendary; he is responsible for helping define the sound of, and jumpstarting the careers of bands as diverse as Devo, The Talking Heads, U2, and Coldplay. His landmark album (with David Byrne) "My Life in the Bush of Ghosts" ushered in an entirely new musical vocabulary and production techniques that are still widely heralded by artists and the recording industry.
